terms.meaning: The source record that shows where a number came from, such as a publication and a page reference.
A display component that shows a value together with its source link, or says no source is on file.
The full source reference for a value, shown in a drawer when a reader clicks it.
The actual outcome of a project, as opposed to what was planned.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and table rules
sections.what: Brings in colours, the slide frame, the table helpers, the evidence wrapper, and the citation hook. The header comment states the rules: nothing is invented, and missing values stay blank.
sections.why: The header comment states the rules that the slide follows.
sections.watch_out: Colours come from a shared file, so changing them there changes this slide and others.

sections.name: capacityField
sections.title: Wrapping capacity for display
sections.what: Turns a project's capacity number into the same shape as other sourced values, with no source link. Returns nothing if the project has no capacity.
sections.why: The comment says capacity has no source in the scan data, so it shows the number with a no-source-on-file note rather than a fake citation.
sections.watch_out: It always returns no source, so readers will see the no-source note for every capacity value.

sections.name: GlossarySlide (part 1)
sections.title: Starting the slide and choosing the unit
sections.what: Receives the slide context, works out one shared capacity unit when all projects that have capacity agree, sets up the citation drawer, and draws the frame with the project count.
sections.why: The comment says the unit appears in the header only when every project agrees, otherwise each cell shows its own unit.
sections.watch_out: The count n includes every project, even those with no numbers, so the count can be higher than the number of filled cells.

sections.name: GlossarySlide (part 2)
sections.title: Table headings
sections.what: Draws the two heading rows: general information on one side, and budget and schedule on the other. The capacity heading adds the shared unit when there is one.
sections.why: Likely reason: groups the columns into general facts and money and time.
sections.watch_out: The heading cells must match the body cells, or the columns shift out of place.

sections.name: GlossarySlide (part 3)
sections.title: Filling each project row
sections.what: For each project, draws name, location, site type, capacity, planned and realised budget, and planned and realised end date. Realised values turn red when they exceed plan, and each value links to its citation.
sections.why: The header says realised values turn red only when they exceed plan.
sections.watch_out: Red colouring depends on the overrun checks in another file, so a change there changes this slide with no edit here. The planned end date and realised end date also cite different source fields.

summary: Builds the Projects Glossary slide: a table with one row per project showing location, site type, capacity, planned and realised budget, and planned and realised schedule end, with each value traceable to its source.
purpose: Gives a reader a per-project reference table in which every number can be traced to a source, or shown honestly as having none on file.
why: The header comment says every budget, schedule, and capacity value goes through the evidence wrapper so the reader can trace it, and that realised values turn red only when they exceed plan.
how: 1. Read the projects from the slide context. 2. Work out the single capacity unit for the header, if all projects share one. 3. Draw the frame with the project count. 4. Draw a two-row table heading. 5. For each project, compute whether budget or schedule overran, format the values, and render each cell through the evidence wrapper with a link to its full citation. 6. Show the footnote and the citation drawer.
inputs: The slide context (`ctx`) with report data (`data.projects`), industry name, industry slug, and page number. Each project's name, location, site type, capacity, budget, and schedule fields.
outputs: A table inside the House frame. Clicking a value opens a full citation drawer for that field.
risks: Capacity has no source record, so its cell shows a value with no citation. Citation field names must match the scan field paths in another file. Projects with missing values show blank cells without warning.
debug: If a cell is blank, check whether the project field is missing. If the red highlighting looks wrong, check `budgetOverran` and `scheduleOverran` in scanTypes. If a citation does not open, check that the field path names match the scan fields file.
